r1-observability-1.summary: Account linking and consent flows via aa-connector started failing at exactly 2026-10-08T13:30:00+00:00 due to an expired mTLS client certificate causing SSL handshakes with aa-fiu-gateway to fail.

findings.statement: The error rate for aa-connector began rising sharply at 2026-10-08T13:30:00+00:00.
The error rate for mobile-bff spiked upward starting at 2026-10-08T13:30:00+00:00.
mTLS client certificate CN=aa-connector.orange.internal expired at 2026-10-08T13:30:00Z.
SSL handshake with aa-fiu-gateway failed due to the expired certificate starting at 2026-10-08T13:30:03+00:00.
Financial information fetch failed for consents due to upstream errors.

open_questions: Are there any other external gateways or dependent clients using similar certificates that might also be affected?

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependencies for aa-connector, mobile-bff, and auth-service. Listed all configuration and deployment changes across the 7-day lookback window, noting that aa-connector was deployed on 2026-10-07 via chg-8692 and other routine deployments occurred prior to the incident onset at ~13:30 on 2026-10-08.

findings.statement: aa-connector depends synchronously on aa-fiu-gateway and user-db.
mobile-bff depends synchronously on aa-connector, auth-service, payments-api, portfolio-service, orders-service, and kyc-service.
auth-service depends synchronously on user-db, redis-session, and otp-provider.
aa-connector received a minor bug fix deploy (v8.18.8) on 2026-10-07T01:22:00+00:00 under change ID chg-8692.
fraud-service and orders-service received routine releases shortly before the incident on 2026-10-08 under chg-9541 and chg-9816.

open_questions: What is the internal state and error rate of the external dependency aa-fiu-gateway since our logs do not cover external vendors directly?
Whether the change in aa-connector (chg-8692) contributed to consent timeouts or if external factors on the AA network are responsible.

hypotheses.title: Expired mTLS Certificate on aa-connector
hypotheses.mechanism: The mTLS client certificate used by aa-connector to authenticate with aa-fiu-gateway expired at 2026-10-08T13:30:00Z. This caused subsequent SSL handshakes to fail, preventing account linking and consent flows.

supporting.note: Shows the exact mTLS client certificate expiration time matching the onset.
Records SSL handshake failures due to expired certificate starting at 13:30:03.
Shows financial information fetch failing for consents due to upstream errors.
Error rate spiked upward at 13:30 due to synchronous dependency on aa-connector.

assumptions: The automated certificate renewal process for aa-connector was either misconfigured or failed to execute prior to expiration.

hypotheses.title: External aa-fiu-gateway Certificate Trust Store Rejection
hypotheses.mechanism: An unexpected policy change or trust store update on the external aa-fiu-gateway rejected valid client connections precisely at 13:30.

supporting.note: SSL handshake failure with external gateway.

contradicting.note: Explicitly proves that the local client certificate expired at the exact onset time.

assumptions: The local certificate expiration warning is coincidental and the remote gateway enforced rejection independently.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: Symptom onset is established at 2026-10-08T13:30:00+00:00. H1 is strongly supported by direct log evidence of local certificate expiration (log-00002) matching the exact time SSL handshakes began failing (log-00551) and error rates surged (metric:aa-connector:error_rate_pct). H2 is retained as a low-probability alternative.

adjustments.reason: Direct log evidence (log-00002) proves the mTLS client certificate expired at 13:30:00Z, perfectly aligning with the onset of SSL handshake failures (log-00551) and the error rate spike on aa-connector.
